newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Large retail chains post mixed sales for August.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Large retail chains post mixed sales for August.

text.p: Large retail chains Thursday posted mixed sales results for August after robust demand for new fashion lines failed to make up for stiff competition and a lack of bargains at many stores.
Cool weather in the East and the launch of new apparel lines by Ralph Lauren and other designers helped department stores ring up strong results, analysts said.
School opened in many markets, lifting sales of backpacks, shoes and fall clothes at discounter Wal-Mart Stores Inc. and moderately priced chains such as J.C. Penney Co. Inc.
But other stores, including Gap Inc., Kmart Corp. and Federated Department Stores Inc., were overlooked by shoppers.

While the wave of going-out-of business sales and bankruptcy filings among retailers has slowed this year, competition for customers is still fierce. Stores such as Gap that did not offer bargains on fall merchandise suffered.
"Expectations got a little inflated," said Michael Exstein of PaineWebber. "The enthusiasm was tempered by reality."

A Dean Witter Reynolds index of same-store sales, or sales at stores open a year or more, rose 3.5 percent. The reading was above last year's 2.4 percent increase, but was weaker than the firm had forecast.

Analysts said retailers should have had an easier time posting big improvements over last year because demand for fall goods was hurt by hot weather in August of 1995. Shares of most major retailers slumped after the sales news.
"I think it's somewhat disappointing," said Patrick McCormack, retail industry analyst at Dean Witter. "You didn't have any blow-out numbers."
San Francisco-based Gap said its same-store sales were flat during August. Analysts had forecast a gain of about 5 to 8 percent.

Sales of denim goods were weak at its flagship Gap chain, the company said. Many of the speciality retailer's competitors advertised special deals on jeans for students heading back to school, which undercut Gap's results.
"We had a weak performance from Gap, particularly in the base five-pocket jeans category," said Warren Hashagen, Gap's chief financial officer.
Gap's shares fell $4.875, or 14 percent, to $29 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.

Cincinnati-based Federated Department Stores Inc., parent of Macy's, Bloomingdale's, and Stern's department stores, also did not offer many bargains on merchandise, a strategy that pressured sales but should help it record strong profits on the goods it did sell. Federated's sales rose 2.5 percent.

Kmart Corp., the nation's second-largest retailer, said its sales rose just 1 percent, which was an improvement from a 3.7 percent drop in July. But Kmart's results trailed competitor Wal-Mart's 3.9 percent gain and the 6 percent increase at discounter Target, a unit of Dayton Hudson Corp.
"While these sales results are improved from July's levels, Kmart's performance remains below plan," said Kmart Chairman and Chief Executive Floyd Hall.
Sales were better at J.C. Penney, up 7 percent, May Department Stores Co., which rose 7.9 percent, and Saks Holdings Inc., whose sales jumped 11.8 percent.

Three popular designers started selling new women's apparel lines at department stores last month: Ralph Lauren's Lauren sportswear line, Tommy Hilfiger's Tommy casual clothing line and Nautica's moderately priced designer line.
"The big news is that women's apparel is quite strong," said Daniel Barry of Merrill Lynch. "As a group, department stores had a stronger month than general merchandisers."
